title: Filling the shoes of Jonathan Groff is no easy feat- but Matt Magnuss...
transcript: Just in time was one of the biggest surprises for me last season. As someone who is not a huge bio jukebox musical fan and didn't really know anything about Bobby Darin, I was really surprised at just how much fun I had. However, so much of the show seemed to hinge on Jonathan Groff's magnetic performance as Bobby Darin, and so with him out all week, I was really excited, but also a little bit nervous to see what the show would be like without him in it. I am happy to say that any skepticism that I had going into the show was very quickly alleviated pretty much the second that Matthew Magnusson stepped on that stage. He has the charm, charisma, and voice needed to really sell this role. And of course, it doesn't hurt that he is incredibly handsome, I was really impressed with how he was able to make this role his own, felt so comfortable with the audience, and had a lot of really great ad lib moments. And overall, this show is just as fun as I remember it. The show's production elements, from its set to lighting to costumes to choreography, are still as stellar as ever. From the second that you walk into that theater, you are transported into a club. The action is happening all around you, and there is truly not a bad seat in the house if you've been wanting to see the show. But the Prices have scared you off. You are in a great hands with Matt Magnusson and tickets are like a third of the price. They have also announced a national tour. And with Groff leaving the show in March, I think the show will be in really great hands with whoever ends up taking over the role. So I'm very excited to see other actors get to put their stamp on this role. And in the meantime, if you have the opportunity to see Matt Magnusson, whether you have seen Groff or not, I absolutely think it is worth it.
classificationReason: Creator attended the show with Matthew Magnusson subbing for Jonathan Groff and shares clear opinions on his performance, as well as the set, lighting, costumes, and choreography of the production.
